_doc: GRANDFATHERED ledger rows whose `git sha` column does not match the `git_sha` recorded inside
their own proof bundle. Read by scripts/programme-rollup.mjs. SHRINK-ONLY: a mismatch that is
not listed here is an integrity failure, and a record here that no longer corresponds to a real
mismatch is ALSO an integrity failure — a stale acknowledgement is the same shape as the thing
it was meant to expose.
WHY RECORDS AND NOT A COUNT. A ceiling of 'four' lets a fifth mismatch move in the moment one of
these is superseded. Each row is named, so the ratchet can only ever be satisfied by the specific
rows it was declared for. This mirrors infra/template-parity-exclusions.yaml, whose own header
makes the same argument: a record for something that does not exist is exactly the stale-record
shape the ratchet refuses.
SURVIVING CLAIMS ONLY. Seven rows in the ledger mismatch, but three of them have been superseded
and are no longer anyone's evidence. The guard walks the collapsed view for the same reason the
BLOCKED-vs-spent rule does — firing on a corrected row punishes the supersession convention this
repo asks people to follow. So exactly one record per cell can ever match, and a duplicate is
refused rather than absorbed.
WHY THESE ARE NOT SIMPLY FIXED. The ledger is append-only and is never corrected in place
(PROGRAMME.md §3). The remedy is a RETRACTED row that supersedes the wrong one plus a re-record,
which is a proof decision with its own evidence — not a lint. These are recorded so the NEXT one
cannot arrive unseen.
THE DRIFT RUNS BOTH WAYS, which is what rules out every benign explanation. hetzner/full and the
two gcp rows name a commit NEWER than the run; aws/full names one OLDER. 'The row is written
after the code moved' cannot cover both. The mechanism is structural: provisioning-e2e.sh takes
`git rev-parse --short HEAD` in the ROLLUP job while the bundle's git_sha is stamped in the LEG
job, so any merge landing between them separates the two.
TWO OF THESE BACK CELLS THE GRID RENDERS PROVEN — gcp/byo (gitops) and gcp/day2. That is why this
is a guard and not a note: a PASS naming a commit its run never executed is unverifiable in
precisely the way an expiring CI run tag was, and every 2026-07-22 row was retracted for that.
